answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each account to post a bond that is slashed if it double-spends or repeatedly defaults on work. A reputation-weighted escrow releases payment only after a counterparty confirms delivery, so creating many identities does not multiply trusted credit: each starts with no history and needs separately funded bonds. The plume of cheap accounts meets a prism of independent checks, while a willow-like reputation grows only through costly, verified transactions. The attacker pays capital and time for every identity, and loses the bond when caught.
